evidence.claim: A large formal room supports a table, several chairs and multiple standing occupants.
A plainer occupied room contains tables, equipment and uniformed personnel.
People coordinate in a corridor at a stated shipboard time.
A long decorated corridor accommodates multiple guards moving in formation.
An exterior sea horizon confirms the vessel is underway.
A deep corridor view shows repeated wall panels and ceiling bands.
A 1010 plaque identifies a corridor-facing suite.
A handheld device is used for coordination while aboard the vessel.
A formal suite contains large furniture and decorative fixed surfaces.
A large ornate panel or door marks an interior boundary.
A bed or couch zone occupies part of a furnished suite.
The 1004 plaque identifies another royal-suite entrance.
Characters coordinate across a tall doorway opening to the corridor.
The corridor supports group movement without single-file restriction.

contradictionsAndQuarantines.subject: Room-number adjacency
contradictionsAndQuarantines.rule: Visible 1010 and 1004 plaques do not prove their relative position.

contradictionsAndQuarantines.subject: Exterior horizon panel
contradictionsAndQuarantines.rule: The sea horizon confirms shipboard travel state but not hull geometry or exact elevation.

unresolvedQuestions: How are 1010 and 1004 positioned relative to one another?
From which exterior elevation is the sea visible?

excludedMaterial.reason: Excluded pages do not independently establish ship evidence.
